name: Cortisol-Hippocampal Cascade

mechanism_chain.description: Architectural stressor exposure (enclosure R_h_ratio < 0.30, acoustic unpredictability, navigational confusion)

data.finding: Room enclosure (R_h_ratio < 0.30) produces elevated cortisol response and slower recovery in TSST paradigm
data.effect: 73% cortisol increase in enclosed vs. open room

data.finding: Low ceiling height correlates with constricted feelings and approach avoidance

justification.backing: Fich's VR paradigm directly demonstrates that architectural parameters (ceiling height, room proportions) modulate the cortisol stress response. This is the architectural translation of the TSST.
justification.qualifier: Effect sizes derived from controlled VR exposure; real-building extrapolation involves occupancy duration, task context, and behavioral adaptation.
justification.rebuttal: Would fail if occupant habituation eliminates architectural stress effects over repeated exposures; or if behavioral adaptation (leaving the space) truncates the physiological response.

mechanism_chain.ceiling_override_rationale: The mechanism or covariance evidence is well-supported and consistent across multiple studies. The confidence exceeds the default warrant ceiling due to replicability, multiple supporting pathways, and/or biological plausibility.

data.finding: HPA cascade: hypothalamic CRH → anterior pituitary ACTH → adrenocortical cortisol synthesis is the canonical stress response pathway

justification.backing: The HPA axis is a constitutive biological pathway. CRH release from the hypothalamus triggers ACTH from the pituitary, which triggers cortisol synthesis in the adrenal cortex. This is basic neuroendocrinology.
justification.qualifier: The pathway is well-established; individual variation in HPA reactivity depends on genetics, prior stress history, and circadian timing.
justification.rebuttal: Would fail if an alternative stress pathway (e.g., direct sympathetic activation without HPA involvement) dominated the cortisol response.

mechanism_chain.ceiling_override_rationale: The mechanism or covariance evidence is well-supported and consistent across multiple studies. The confidence exceeds the default warrant ceiling due to replicability, multiple supporting pathways, and/or biological plausibility.

mechanism_chain.description: → Cortisol elevation (onset lag: 20 min; λ = 0.035 min⁻¹)

data.finding: Peak salivary cortisol at 15-25 min post-stressor (modal value 20 min); recovery follows first-order exponential with half-life ~20 min
Two-compartment model: onset delay τ_onset follows first-order delay; recovery C(t) = C_peak × e^{−λ(t−t_peak)}, λ ≈ 0.035 min⁻¹

justification.backing: Kirschbaum's TSST protocol established the canonical cortisol time course. The onset lag reflects HPA cascade transport and synthesis delays; the recovery rate reflects cortisol clearance kinetics.
justification.qualifier: Elderly subjects show 30-40% slower recovery (λ ≈ 0.022 min⁻¹). High-reactivity individuals show earlier peak (15 min).
justification.rebuttal: Would fail if salivary cortisol timing differs substantially from plasma cortisol or brain glucocorticoid receptor occupancy.

mechanism_chain.description: → Glucocorticoid binding at hippocampal GR/MR receptors

data.finding: Hippocampus has highest density of glucocorticoid receptors (GR) and mineralocorticoid receptors (MR) in the brain; cortisol binds both with different affinities

justification.backing: The hippocampus is the primary site of cortisol action in the brain. MR binds cortisol at low levels (tonic); GR binds at elevated levels (stress). This is basic neuroendocrine anatomy.
justification.qualifier: The constitutive pathway is well-established; the functional consequences depend on dose, duration, and receptor occupancy kinetics.
justification.rebuttal: Would fail if cortisol brain effects are mediated primarily by non-hippocampal structures (amygdala, PFC); these pathways exist but hippocampal effects dominate for spatial memory.

mechanism_chain.ceiling_override_rationale: The mechanism or covariance evidence is well-supported and consistent across multiple studies. The confidence exceeds the default warrant ceiling due to replicability, multiple supporting pathways, and/or biological plausibility.

data.finding: Acute cortisone administration (25 mg) impairs declarative memory retrieval in healthy subjects
data.paradigm: Randomized controlled trial with word list recall

data.finding: Cortisol elevation within 20-40 nmol/L range produces linear impairment of hippocampal-dependent memory; plateaus at higher levels

justification.backing: De Quervain's RCT directly demonstrates that acute cortisol elevation impairs memory retrieval. Lupien's review establishes the dose-response relationship and identifies the hippocampus as the vulnerable structure.
justification.qualifier: Effect is specific to retrieval, not encoding. Acute effects are transient; memory returns as cortisol clears. Individual variation in vulnerability is substantial.
justification.rebuttal: Would fail if acute cortisol enhances encoding (which it does) in a way that offsets retrieval impairment; the net effect depends on task timing relative to cortisol peak.

mechanism_chain.description: → Chronic (repeated activation >4/day): CA3 dendritic retraction, hippocampal volume reduction

data.finding: Chronic glucocorticoid elevation produces dendritic retraction in CA3 pyramidal neurons; reversible with 10-day recovery
Human longitudinal imaging: ≥4 stress activations per day associated with accelerated hippocampal volume loss
data.effect: Volume reduction correlates with cumulative cortisol exposure

justification.backing: McEwen's chronic stress model demonstrates the mechanism: repeated glucocorticoid exposure causes CA3 dendritic retraction. Lupien's human data confirm the threshold (~4 activations/day) for cumulative damage.
justification.qualifier: Structural effects require weeks to months of sustained activation. Effects are partially reversible with stress reduction. Individual resilience varies.
justification.rebuttal: Would fail if human chronic stress effects differ substantially from rodent models; or if hippocampal neurogenesis compensates for chronic damage.

mechanism_chain.ceiling_override_rationale: The mechanism or covariance evidence is well-supported and consistent across multiple studies. The confidence exceeds the default warrant ceiling due to replicability, multiple supporting pathways, and/or biological plausibility.

mechanism_chain.description: → Progressive spatial memory and navigation impairment

data.finding: Hippocampal volume correlates with spatial navigation performance; volume reduction associated with wayfinding impairment
Elderly with high cortisol exposure show greater spatial memory decline than age-matched controls
data.effect: Cortisol × age interaction on spatial cognition

justification.backing: The hippocampus is the substrate for cognitive mapping and spatial navigation. Structural damage to the hippocampus impairs these functions. This connects T6 to the spatial navigation templates (SS1, SS2, T14).
justification.qualifier: Spatial impairment is a downstream consequence; compensatory strategies (external aids, verbal directions) can partially offset hippocampal damage.
justification.rebuttal: Would fail if spatial navigation relies primarily on non-hippocampal structures (striatal route learning) in the built environment; this shifts the vulnerability away from T6's mechanism.
